Macros

#define SNICHOLLS_EMPTY_BASES
 Makes every empty base cost nothing on MSVC too (__declspec(empty_bases)); empty elsewhere.
#define SNICHOLLS_RESULT_THROW   1
 Unwrap-on-error policy: 1 throws snicholls::bad_result_access, 0 prints and calls std::terminate.
#define SNICHOLLS_RESULT_HAS_EXCEPTIONS   0
 1 when the compiler has exceptions (try_invoke can catch, rethrow() can throw), else 0.
#define SNICHOLLS_RESULT_HAS_STATEMENT_EXPRESSIONS   0
 1 when SNICHOLLS_TRY(expr) (a GNU statement expression) is available (GCC, Clang); 0 on MSVC.
#define SNICHOLLS_RESULT_NO_UNIQUE_ADDRESS   [[no_unique_address]]
 [[no_unique_address]], spelled so MSVC honours it too (it ignores the standard spelling).
#define SNICHOLLS_TRY_ASSIGN(decl, ...)
 Portable ? as a statement: declares decl from the value of expr, or returns its error.
#define SNICHOLLS_TRY_VOID(...)
 Portable ? as a statement, discarding the value: returns the error of expr if there is one.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_MAJOR   0
 Major version of snicholls-core.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_MINOR   5
 Minor version of snicholls-core.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_PATCH   1
 Patch version of snicholls-core.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_CHECK(major, minor, patch)
 Encode a version as one integer the preprocessor can compare.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION    SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_CHECK(SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_MAJOR, SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_MINOR, SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_PATCH)
 This version of snicholls-core, encoded by SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_CHECK.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_STRINGIFY_(x)
 Implementation detail of SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_STRING: stringise a token.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_STRINGIFY(x)
 Implementation detail of SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_STRING: expand, then stringise.
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_VERSION_STRING
 This version of snicholls-core as a string literal, "major.minor.patch".
#define SNICHOLLS_CORE_REQUIRE_VERSION(major, minor, patch)
 Fail to compile unless snicholls-core is at least major.minor.patch.

Detailed Description

The vocabulary types and compile-time reflection shared by the snicholls libraries.

Everything in this group is header-only, standard-library-only and C++20. There is no I/O, no threading, no networking and no codec here, by rule (CLAUDE.md "What belongs here"); the libraries that pin core supply those.

◆ SNICHOLLS_RESULT_THROW

#define SNICHOLLS_RESULT_THROW   1

Unwrap-on-error policy: 1 throws snicholls::bad_result_access, 0 prints and calls std::terminate.

1 is the default when exceptions are on, 0 under -fno-exceptions. It is a whole-program switch: set it for the whole program (-DSNICHOLLS_RESULT_THROW=0), never per file. Per call site, value_or_throw() and unwrap_or_terminate() choose explicitly whatever the policy.

The two policies put snicholls::result in different inline namespaces (snicholls::result_throws / snicholls::result_terminates). Mixing them is a link error wherever a result appears in a signature shared by translation units built with different policies; otherwise (a function that only uses results inside its body, an inline function, a template) it is an ODR violation that nothing diagnoses. On MSVC a #pragma detect_mismatch("snicholls_result_throw", ...) makes any mix a link error; GCC and Clang have no equivalent, so the whole-program rule stands.

using snicholls::meta::permutations_t = typename detail::permutations_impl<List, R>::type

Every distinct ordering of R elements of List: permutations_t<<a, b>> is <<a, b>, <b, a>>.

Rows are in lexicographic order, with types ranked by first appearance. A repeated type gives each distinct row once (<a, a, b> has 3 rows, not 6), and R above the size gives no rows. ◆ thread_t

template<typename Expression, template< typename... > class Head = type_list, typename Spec = thread_all>
using snicholls::meta::thread_t = typename detail::thread_expression<Expression, Head, Spec>::type

Mathematica's Thread[f[args], h, spec]: thread_t<f<type_list<a, b>, x>> is type_list<f<a, x>, f<b, x>>.

f is threaded over the arguments whose head is Head, and the result has that head. Other arguments are repeated. Threaded arguments must be of one length. With nothing to thread, the result is the expression itself. thread_t<type_list<L1, L2>> is the transpose, as in Wolfram. One level only. As Wolfram warns of Thread evaluating first, naming f<type_list<...>, x> must be harmless: where f is an alias or is constrained, use thread_with_t, its MapThread-like form.

Template Parameters
ExpressionThe expression: any specialisation of a template of types.
HeadThe head to thread over: type_list, std::tuple or any other template of types.
SpecWhich arguments: thread_all, thread_none, thread_first, thread_at, thread_range.

void snicholls::for_each_set_partition ( F && f)
constexprnoexcept

Call f(block_of, blocks) for every partition of N elements into blocks.

block_of[i] is the block of element i, numbered in order of first appearance (a restricted growth string: block_of[0] is 0 and each entry is at most one more than the largest before it), and blocks is how many there are. The first partition is one block, the last is every element alone.

◆ for_each_stationary_resample()

template<full_range_generator G, typename F>
void snicholls::stats::for_each_stationary_resample ( std::size_t n,
double mean_block_length,
std::size_t resamples,
G & g,
F && f )

Call f(indices) for each resample of the stationary bootstrap (Politis and Romano), for time series.

Each resample is a run of blocks: a block starts at a random observation and continues to the next one (wrapping round) with probability 1 - 1/mean_block_length, so block lengths are geometric with that mean and the resampled series is stationary. Autocorrelation within a block is kept.

◆ is_business_day()

bool snicholls::is_business_day ( std::chrono::sys_days d)
constexprnoexcept

Whether d is Monday to Friday.

Overview

Weekday arithmetic on std::chrono calendar types: a Monday-to-Friday calendar (no holidays). See the file description above.

Relationships
  • snicholls::add_business_days, snicholls::business_days_between, snicholls::next_weekday, snicholls::add_months.
  • Group: snicholls-core.
Implementations and variants

None: a single implementation.

Guarantees and contracts
  • O(1), constexpr, noexcept.
Errors

None.

Examples
int main()
{
using namespace std::chrono;
int failures = 0;
const auto check = [&](const char* what, bool ok) {
std::cout << (ok ? " ok " : " FAIL ") << what << '\n';
failures += !ok;
};
const auto ymd = [](sys_days d) { return snicholls::to_string(year_month_day(d)); };
const sys_days friday = sys_days{2024y / May / 3};
const sys_days saturday = friday + days(1);
const sys_days monday = friday + days(3);
std::cout << "Friday " << ymd(friday) << " + 3 business days = " << ymd(snicholls::add_business_days(friday, 3)) << '\n';
check("weekend / business day", snicholls::is_weekend(Saturday) && snicholls::is_weekend(Sunday) && !snicholls::is_weekend(Friday) &&
snicholls::is_business_day(friday) && !snicholls::is_business_day(saturday));
check("Friday + 1 = Monday, + 3 = Wednesday", snicholls::add_business_days(friday, 1) == monday &&
snicholls::add_business_days(friday, 3) == monday + days(2));
check("Saturday + 1 = Monday, Sunday + 1 = Monday", snicholls::add_business_days(saturday, 1) == monday &&
snicholls::add_business_days(saturday + days(1), 1) == monday);
check("Monday - 1 = Friday, Saturday - 1 = Friday, Sunday - 2 = Thursday",
snicholls::add_business_days(monday, -1) == friday && snicholls::add_business_days(saturday, -1) == friday &&
snicholls::add_business_days(saturday + days(1), -2) == friday - days(1));
check("+10 and -10 are two weeks", snicholls::add_business_days(monday, 10) == monday + days(14) &&
snicholls::add_business_days(monday, -10) == monday - days(14));
check("n == 0 leaves the day unchanged", snicholls::add_business_days(saturday, 0) == saturday);
check("business days in [Friday, next Friday) = 5, reversed = -5, across 1970 too",
snicholls::business_days_between(friday, friday + days(7)) == 5 && snicholls::business_days_between(friday + days(7), friday) == -5 &&
snicholls::business_days_between(sys_days{1969y / December / 26}, sys_days{1970y / January / 2}) == 5);
std::cout << "last Friday before " << ymd(friday) << " = " << ymd(snicholls::previous_weekday(friday, Friday)) << '\n';
check("previous / next weekday are strict", snicholls::previous_weekday(friday, Friday) == friday - days(7) &&
snicholls::previous_weekday(monday, Friday) == friday &&
snicholls::next_weekday(friday, Monday) == monday &&
snicholls::next_weekday(monday, Monday) == monday + days(7));
std::cout << "2024-01-31 + 1 month = " << snicholls::to_string(snicholls::add_months(2024y / January / 31, 1)) << '\n';
check("add_months clamps to the end of the month", snicholls::add_months(2024y / January / 31, 1) == 2024y / February / 29 &&
snicholls::add_months(2024y / March / 31, -1) == 2024y / February / 29 &&
snicholls::add_months(2024y / March / 15, -3) == 2023y / December / 15);
std::cout << (failures == 0 ? "OK\n" : "FAILED\n");
return failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
Performance

Not benchmarked.

  • Demo: demos/time/business_days_demo.cpp.

Known issues and gotchas
  • No holiday calendars: weekends only.

◆ optimal_block_length()

block_lengths snicholls::stats::optimal_block_length ( std::span< const double > x)
inlinenodiscard

Estimate the block lengths a dependent series needs, from its autocorrelations (the same as Python arch's optimal_block_length).

Autocorrelations are taken until max(5, log10 n) in a row are insignificant; a flat-top kernel over twice that many lags estimates the long-run variance and its derivative, whose ratio sets the length. An independent series gives about 1; a persistent one, tens. Capped at min(3 sqrt(n), n / 3).

Parameters
xThe series, at least 8 observations.
Returns
The two lengths.

nodiscardconstexpr

Mathematica's Outer[f, list1, list2, ...]: f of every combination, nested one level per list.

outer(f, {a, b}, {x, y}) is {{f(a, x), f(a, y)}, {f(b, x), f(b, y)}}. Each call is resolved on its own, so an overloaded picks a branch per pair of types. A level is a std::array when its list was one (and not empty), otherwise a std::tuple; the type-level form is meta::outer_with_t.

◆ sun_position()

template<utc_duration D>
solar_position snicholls::sun_position ( const utc< D > & t)
nodiscardnoexcept

The sun's position at instant t.

Overview

NOAA's solar position algorithm (the NOAA Solar Calculator spreadsheets, after Meeus, "Astronomical Algorithms"): accurate to about 0.01 degree in declination and a few seconds in the equation of time for 1800..2100, far better than the one-line approximations used in UIs. Drives the world clock's day/night map. UTC here is snicholls::utc (Unix time); the ~1 minute between UT1 and UTC-with-leap-seconds is below this use's resolution.

Relationships

Used by world-clock displays (day and night per city). Group: snicholls-core.

Implementations and variants

None (functions).

Guarantees and contracts
  • Thread safety: pure functions.
  • Exception safety: noexcept (the terminator may throw std::bad_alloc).
  • Complexity: O(1); the terminator O(points).
Errors

None.

Examples
const snicholls::solar_position sun = snicholls::sun_position(snicholls::utc<>::now());

◆ tie()

template<typename S>
requires plain_struct<S>
auto snicholls::tie ( S & s)
constexprnoexcept

References to every member of a plain struct: a std::tuple of references.

Overview

The first of the struct / tuple conversions; all are summarised in the file description above. Use them at boundaries with tuple-based code (std::apply, comparison through std::tuple, C APIs, legacy structs).

Relationships
  • snicholls::to_tuple, snicholls::from_tuple; member count from snicholls::member_count_v.
  • A consuming library may add overloads of the same names for its own objects.
  • Module: snicholls-core.
Implementations and variants
Function From To
tie struct (lvalue) tuple of references
to_tuple struct tuple of values
from_tuple<S> tuple-like struct
Guarantees and contracts
  • Everything is constexpr. tie is always noexcept; every other conversion is noexcept exactly when the copies, moves and assignments it performs are (a std::string copy may throw).
  • Strict input: sizes must match exactly and arithmetic conversions must not narrow (compile-time errors with a snicholls:: message).
Errors

Only what the element copies throw (std::bad_alloc); misuse is a compile error.

Examples
auto refs = snicholls::tie(o);
std::get<1>(refs).qty = 200;
std::get<2>(refs) = "twap";
snicholls::tie(o) = std::make_tuple(8L, leg_row{10.25, 300}, std::string("close"));
// to_tuple / from_tuple: values out, a struct back in. Strict: sizes must match, no narrowing.
const auto values = snicholls::to_tuple(o); // std::tuple<long, leg_row, std::string>
const order_row copy = snicholls::from_tuple<order_row>(values);
const leg_row from_pair = snicholls::from_tuple<leg_row>(std::make_pair(1.5, 2));
Performance

tie, to_tuple and from_tuple are benchmarked like for like against hand-written member access (benchmarks/reflect/struct_tuple_benchmark.cpp, with a fairness check); see BENCHMARKS.md.

Tests and demos
  • Tests: tests/reflect/struct_tuple_test.cpp; compile-fail cases (size mismatch, narrowing) in tests/compile_fail/struct_tuple_*.cpp.
  • Demo: demos/reflect/struct_tuple_demo.cpp.
  • Benchmark: benchmarks/reflect/struct_tuple_benchmark.cpp.
Dependencies

CMake target snicholls::core; standard library only.

Known issues and gotchas
  • Plain structs: no reference members, C arrays (use std::array), bit-fields, base classes or unions; up to SNICHOLLS_MAX_STRUCT_MEMBERS (256) members.
  • Migrating from a to_tuple<N>(s) / to_struct<S>(tuple) pair: they are snicholls::to_tuple(s) and snicholls::from_tuple<S>(tuple).
Status

Stable. Rules: CLAUDE.md, "Struct / tuple conversion rules".

template<utc_duration D>

char * last,
const utc< D > & t,
int precision )
constexprnoexcept

Writes t as RFC 3339 text into [first, last) with precision fraction digits.

Overview

RFC 3339 text for snicholls::utc in the style of std::to_chars / std::from_chars: no allocation, no locale, no exceptions, constexpr, exact round trips. See the file description above.

Relationships
  • Reverse: snicholls::from_chars, snicholls::parse_utc; strings: snicholls::to_text, snicholls::to_string; options snicholls::parse_options.
  • Group: snicholls-core.
Implementations and variants

None: a single implementation.

Guarantees and contracts
  • noexcept, no allocation; output length snicholls::rfc3339_length(digits).
Errors

Returns std::to_chars_result with errc::value_too_large if the buffer is too small; parsing reports through snicholls::parse_result.

Examples
int main()
{
using namespace std::chrono;
using namespace std::chrono_literals;
using snicholls::utc;
int failures = 0;
const auto check = [&](const char* what, bool ok) {
std::cout << (ok ? " ok " : " FAIL ") << what << '\n';
failures += !ok;
};
const auto show = [](std::string_view label, std::errc ec) {
std::cout << " " << label << " -> " << (ec == std::errc{} ? "ok" : std::make_error_code(ec).message()) << '\n';
};
// ---- formatting ----
const utc<> t = utc<>::from_unix_nanos(1714486985123456789);
char buf[snicholls::max_chars_v<nanoseconds>];
const auto [end, ec] = snicholls::to_chars(buf, buf + sizeof buf, t);
std::cout << "to_chars: " << std::string_view(buf, static_cast<std::size_t>(end - buf)) << '\n';
check("to_chars writes 30 chars, ns precision", ec == std::errc{} && end - buf == 30);
check("to_text(t).view()", snicholls::to_text(t).view() == "2024-04-30T14:23:05.123456789Z");
check("precision 0, 3, 1 (floored)", snicholls::to_string(t, 0) == "2024-04-30T14:23:05Z" &&
snicholls::to_string(t, 3) == "2024-04-30T14:23:05.123Z" &&
snicholls::to_string(t, 1) == "2024-04-30T14:23:05.1Z");
check("coarser types print their own digits", snicholls::to_string(utc<milliseconds>(floor<milliseconds>(t.sys_time()))) == "2024-04-30T14:23:05.123Z" &&
snicholls::to_string(utc<seconds>{}) == "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z" &&
snicholls::to_string(utc<days>{}) == "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z");
check("zero-padded when finer than the type", snicholls::to_string(utc<seconds>{}, 2) == "1970-01-01T00:00:00.00Z");
check("before 1970 is floored", snicholls::to_string(utc<>::from_unix_nanos(-1), 3) == "1969-12-31T23:59:59.999Z");
check("buffer too small: value_too_large", snicholls::to_chars(buf, buf + 29, t).ec == std::errc::value_too_large);
check("precision 10: invalid_argument", snicholls::to_chars(buf, buf + sizeof buf, t, 10).ec == std::errc::invalid_argument);
const auto year_12000 = utc<seconds>(sys_days{year(12000) / January / 1});
const auto year_minus_1 = utc<seconds>(sys_days{year(-1) / January / 1});
check("years outside 0000..9999: value_too_large, empty text",
snicholls::to_chars(buf, buf + sizeof buf, year_12000).ec == std::errc::value_too_large &&
snicholls::to_chars(buf, buf + sizeof buf, opaque(utc<microseconds>(year_minus_1))).ec == std::errc::value_too_large &&
!snicholls::to_text(year_12000) && snicholls::to_string(year_12000).empty() &&
snicholls::to_chars(buf, buf + sizeof buf, utc<days>::max()).ec == std::errc::value_too_large);
std::ostringstream os;
os << t;
std::ostringstream bad;
bad << year_12000;
check("operator<< writes the text; failbit when it cannot", os.str() == snicholls::to_string(t) && bad.fail());
const snicholls::rfc3339_text epoch_text = snicholls::to_text(utc<seconds>{}); // the view below refers into it
const std::string_view view = epoch_text;
check("rfc3339_text converts to string_view", view == "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z");
// ---- parsing (strict RFC 3339 by default) ----
const auto r = snicholls::parse_utc("2024-04-30T10:23:05.123456789-04:00");
std::cout << "parse_utc(\"2024-04-30T10:23:05.123456789-04:00\") = " << *r << '\n';
check("offsets are applied", r && *r == t);
check("t, z and space separators", snicholls::parse_utc("2024-04-30t14:23:05.123456789z").value() == t &&
snicholls::parse_utc("2024-04-30 14:23:05.123456789Z").value() == t);
for (const char* s : {"2024-04-30T14:23Z", "2024-02-30T00:00:00Z", "2024-04-30T14:23:05", "2024-04-30T14:23:05+0100",
"2024-04-30T14:23:05.Z", "2024-04-30T14:23:05+24:00", "2024-04-30T14:23:05Zjunk",
"1600-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-04-30T14:23:05.1234567891Z", "2016-12-31T23:59:60Z",
"2016-12-31T23:58:60Z", "2024-04-30T14:23:05+01", "2024-04-30T14:23:05+01:0"})
show(s, snicholls::parse_utc(std::string_view(s)).error());
check("missing seconds rejected (never silently zeroed)", snicholls::parse_utc("2024-04-30T14:23Z").error() == std::errc::invalid_argument);
check("invalid date rejected", snicholls::parse_utc("2024-02-30T00:00:00Z").error() == std::errc::invalid_argument);

// parse_result: has_value / error / value_or / value() throwing snicholls::utc_error.
const auto bad_result = snicholls::parse_utc("not a time");
const auto range_result = snicholls::parse_utc("1600-01-01T00:00:00Z");
check("value_or", bad_result.value_or(utc<>::max()) == utc<>::max() && r.value_or(utc<>{}) == t);
try {
(void)bad_result.value();
check("value() throws", false);
} catch (const snicholls::utc_error& e) {
std::cout << " value() threw: " << e.what() << '\n';
check("value() throws snicholls::utc_error(invalid_argument)", e.code() == std::errc::invalid_argument);
}
try {
(void)range_result.value();
check("value() throws", false);
} catch (const snicholls::utc_error& e) {
check("value() throws snicholls::utc_error(result_out_of_range)", e.code() == std::errc::result_out_of_range);
}
// Compile-time literal.
using namespace snicholls::literals;
constexpr utc<> literal = "2024-04-30T14:23:05.123456789Z"_utc;
static_assert(literal.unix_nanos() == 1714486985123456789);
check("\"...\"_utc is checked at compile time", literal == t);
std::cout << (failures == 0 ? "OK\n" : "FAILED\n");
return failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
Performance

Release, 4096 instants in 2000..2030, median of 10, ns per value (macOS AppleClang 17 / Ubuntu clang 18; date not recorded): snicholls::to_chars 29 / 22 (std::format_to_n 1310 / 339); snicholls::to_string 73-85 / 33-39 (std::format 1492 / 361); snicholls::from_chars (strict, validated) 29-32 / 27 (sscanf + timegm 6674 / 461); Unix ms round trip 3.1 vs raw std::chrono 3.1 (zero overhead). The benchmark is benchmarks/time/utc_benchmark.cpp (not on Windows: its baselines are POSIX).

◆ to_string_view()

template<string_like S>
string_view_t< S > snicholls::to_string_view ( const S & s)
constexprnoexcept

Zero-copy view of any text sequence, keeping its character traits.

Overview

Uniform, zero-copy, allocation-free access to every code-unit sequence classified by reflect/string_traits.hpp. The function table is in the file description above.

Relationships
  • Siblings: snicholls::length_of, snicholls::c_str_of, snicholls::as_bytes_view; types: snicholls::string_view_t.
  • Module: snicholls-core.
Implementations and variants

None: a single implementation.

Guarantees and contracts
  • noexcept, no allocation, O(1) except a C* (one strlen). A null C* is the empty string (never UB).
Errors

None.

Examples
int main()
{
using demo::check;
using namespace std::string_view_literals;
std::cout << "to_string_view / length_of over every text carrier:\n";
const char* ptr = "pointer";
const char* null = nullptr;
char buffer[] = "buffer";
const std::string str = "std::string";
const std::vector<char> vec{'v', 'e', 'c'};
const std::array<char, 5> arr{'a', 'r', 'r', 'a', 'y'};
const std::span<const char, 5> fixed_span(arr);
constexpr snicholls::fixed_string name("price");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(ptr) == "pointer" && snicholls::length_of(ptr) == 7, "const char*: strlen, O(n)");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(null).empty() && snicholls::length_of(null) == 0, "null const char*: empty, not UB");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(buffer) == "buffer" && snicholls::length_of(buffer) == 6, "char[7]: N-1 code units");
check(snicholls::to_string_view("a\0b") == "a\0b"sv, "string literal keeps embedded NULs (length 3)");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(str).data() == str.data(), "std::string: same data(), no copy");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(vec) == "vec" && snicholls::length_of(vec) == 3, "std::vector<char>");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(arr) == "array" && snicholls::length_of(arr) == 5, "std::array<char, 5>: compile-time length");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(fixed_span) == "array", "std::span<const char, 5>");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(std::string_view("view")) == "view", "std::string_view");
static_assert(snicholls::to_string_view(name) == "price" && snicholls::length_of(name) == 5);
check(snicholls::to_string_view(name) == "price", "snicholls::fixed_string (constexpr)");
check(snicholls::to_string_view(u"€") == u"€" && snicholls::length_of(u"€") == 1, "char16_t literal");
check(snicholls::length_of(u8"€") == 3, "char8_t: lengths are code units (U+20AC is 3 in UTF-8)");
check(demo::key_length("px") + demo::key_length(str) + demo::key_length(name) == 2 + 11 + 5,
"one generic function accepts every carrier");
std::cout << "\nc_str_of for C APIs (NUL-terminated carriers only):\n";
char out[32];
std::snprintf(out, sizeof out, "%s|%s|%s", snicholls::c_str_of(str), snicholls::c_str_of(name), snicholls::c_str_of(null));
check(out == "std::string|price|"sv, "std::string, fixed_string, null pointer -> \"\"");
check(snicholls::c_str_of(ptr) == ptr && snicholls::c_str_of(buffer) == buffer, "pointer and array pass straight through");
std::cout << "\nas_bytes_view over byte sequences and one-byte text:\n";
const std::vector<std::uint8_t> u8{1, 2, 3};
const std::array<std::byte, 2> raw{std::byte{10}, std::byte{20}};
const unsigned char packet[3] = {4, 0, 5}; // a byte array has no terminator: all 3 bytes
check(demo::checksum(u8) == 6, "std::vector<std::uint8_t>");
check(demo::checksum(raw) == 30, "std::array<std::byte, 2> (constexpr-capable: no cast)");
check(demo::checksum(packet) == 9 && snicholls::length_of(packet) == 3, "unsigned char[3]: length N");
check(demo::checksum("AB") == 65 + 66, "char text: its bytes, without the terminator");
check(snicholls::as_bytes_view(null).empty(), "null const char*: empty span");
static_assert(!snicholls::byte_viewable<std::u16string>, "wide text bytes are endian-dependent");
std::cout << " std::u16string is byte_viewable: " << std::boolalpha << snicholls::byte_viewable<std::u16string> << '\n';
std::cout << (demo::ok ? "\nOK\n" : "\nFAILED\n");
return demo::ok ? 0 : 1;
}

◆ variance_ratio_test()

test_result snicholls::stochastic::variance_ratio_test ( std::span< const double > y,
std::size_t q )
inlinenodiscard

Lo and MacKinlay's variance ratio test of the random walk (martingale) hypothesis, robust to heteroskedasticity.

Under a martingale the variance of q-step moves is q times that of one-step moves. The statistic is the standardised VR(q) - 1 from overlapping q-step moves, debiased; the p-value is two-sided. The same as Python arch's VarianceRatio(y, lags=q).

Parameters
yThe levels (log prices), at least q + 2.
qThe horizon, at least 2.
Returns
The z statistic and its p-value.

◆ member_count_v

template<plain_aggregate S>
std::size_t snicholls::member_count_v = member_count<S>::value
inlineconstexpr

The member count of a plain aggregate struct, detected at compile time.

Overview

So call sites never pass N (snicholls::to_tuple(s), not to_tuple<11>(s)). The technique (as Boost.PFR: the largest N for which S{x0, ..., xN-1} is valid, by binary search) is in the file description above.

Relationships
  • Used by snicholls::tie, snicholls::to_tuple and snicholls::from_tuple (reflect/struct_tuple.hpp).
  • Module: snicholls-core.
Implementations and variants

None: a single implementation.

Guarantees and contracts
  • Compile time only; cost logarithmic in SNICHOLLS_MAX_STRUCT_MEMBERS (256).
Errors

Reference members are a clear compile error.

Examples
struct quote { long id; double px; };
static_assert(snicholls::member_count_v<quote> == 2);
// Greedy constructors, move-only and const members, nested aggregates and std::array each count as one.
struct row {
std::optional<int> maybe;
std::variant<int, std::string> either;
std::unique_ptr<int> owned;
const int fixed;
quote nested;
std::array<int, 3> triple;
};
static_assert(snicholls::member_count_v<row> == 6);
Performance

Not benchmarked.

Tests and demos
  • Tests: tests/reflect/member_count_test.cpp; compile-fail cases (reference member, over the limit) in tests/compile_fail/member_count_*.cpp.
  • Demo: demos/reflect/member_count_demo.cpp.
Dependencies

CMake target snicholls::core; <cstddef>, <type_traits>, <utility>.

Known issues and gotchas
  • C arrays are miscounted (use std::array); bit-fields, base classes and unions are not supported.
Status

Stable. Rules: CLAUDE.md, "Struct / tuple conversion rules".

Sa plain aggregate struct.
